input.requirements_spec: See C1-04 gold standard output — structured spec for the two-level review workflow (brand review → compliance review) with state machine, 7 user stories, edge cases, and NFRs.

existing_services: User Service: user profiles, authentication, roles (creator/brand/admin). Access via UserRepository.
Campaign Service: campaign CRUD, state machine (draft→active→completed). Campaigns own submissions.
Application Service: creator applications to campaigns, acceptance workflow. Accepted creators can submit content.
Content Submission Service: content draft CRUD with version tracking (v1, v2, v3). Submissions have a status field, media references, and auto-validation pipeline.
Notification Service: async push notifications via Celery task queue. Accepts (user_id, template_id, payload).
Payment Service: wallet, transactions, settlement batch processing.
system_context.tech_stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async), PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, Pydantic v2
system_context.architecture_patterns: Layered architecture: Model → Repository → Service → API. Dependency injection via FastAPI Depends. Custom exception classes (NotFoundError, ConflictError, ForbiddenError, ValidationError) mapped to HTTP responses. Pydantic schemas split into Create/Update/Response. Pagination via PaginatedResponse[T]. Soft delete with is_deleted flag. UUID primary keys. TimestampMixin for created_at/updated_at.
constraints: All new tables must use the existing Base, TimestampMixin, and SoftDeleteMixin from app.models.base
All new endpoints must be registered under /api/v1/ via the existing router pattern
Auth is via X-User-Id header → get_current_user dependency. Role checks via require_role() dependency.
Async notifications must use Celery tasks (fire-and-forget), never blocking the request path
Database-level locking is available via SELECT FOR UPDATE (PostgreSQL)

module_design.overview: The review workflow introduces two new models (Review, ReviewComment), plus a ReviewAuditLog for immutable audit trail. The architecture follows a two-level sequential approval chain: content submissions first go through brand review, then automatically advance to compliance review upon brand approval. Each level is handled by the same Review model distinguished by a review_type enum. A single ReviewService orchestrates both levels, enforcing state preconditions, revision limits, and concurrency guards.

new_files.purpose: Review, ReviewComment, and ReviewAuditLog SQLAlchemy models with enums for ReviewType and ReviewDecision
Pydantic schemas: ReviewCreate, ReviewDecisionUpdate, ReviewCommentCreate, ReviewResponse, ReviewCommentResponse, ReviewAuditLogResponse
ReviewRepository: CRUD for reviews, comments, and audit log entries. Includes get_active_review_for_submission() with SELECT FOR UPDATE locking.

ReviewService: orchestrates the two-level review flow. Enforces state machine transitions, revision limits, concurrency guards. Integrates with ContentSubmission service for status updates and Notification service for async alerts.
Review API router: endpoints for listing reviews, submitting decisions, adding comments

modified_files.change: Add imports for Review, ReviewComment, ReviewAuditLog

module_design.architecture_notes: The two-level chain is NOT modeled as two separate workflows. Instead, a single Review model uses a review_type enum (brand_review | compliance_review). When a brand review results in 'approved', the ReviewService automatically creates a new Review record of type compliance_review and transitions the submission to 'pending_compliance'. This keeps the model simple while supporting the sequential chain.

tables.notes: This table is append-only. No UPDATE or DELETE operations are permitted at the application layer. The SoftDeleteMixin is NOT applied to this model.

integration_points.interaction: ReviewService calls SubmissionService.update_status() to transition submission status (e.g., pending_brand_review → brand_approved → pending_compliance → ready_to_publish). The submission service owns the status field; the review service requests transitions and the submission service validates them against its own state machine.
integration_points.interface: Internal method call (same microservice). SubmissionService.update_status(submission_id: str, new_status: SubmissionStatus, actor_id: str) → raises ConflictError if transition is invalid.

integration_points.interaction: After each review decision, ReviewService dispatches an async Celery task to notify the affected party. Fire-and-forget — notification failure does not roll back the review action.
integration_points.interface: Celery task: send_notification.delay(user_id=str, template_id=str, payload=dict). Templates: 'review_revision_requested', 'review_brand_approved', 'review_compliance_rejected', 'review_ready_to_publish', 'review_escalated'.

integration_points.interaction: ReviewService uses the existing get_current_user dependency to authenticate and authorize reviewers. Role checks (brand vs admin) are enforced via require_role().
integration_points.interface: Existing FastAPI dependency: CurrentUser, require_role('brand'), require_role('admin').

technical_decisions.decision: Sequential two-level review (brand → compliance) using a single Review model with review_type enum
alternatives_considered: Two separate models (BrandReview, ComplianceReview): rejected because it doubles the code with nearly identical schemas and logic.
Parallel review (brand and compliance simultaneously): rejected per CQ-4.1 — creates conflict resolution complexity and wastes compliance resources if brand rejects.
technical_decisions.justification: A single Review model with review_type enum keeps the data model simple while cleanly separating the two review levels. The ReviewService handles the automatic brand_approved → create compliance_review transition internally.

technical_decisions.decision: Database-level partial unique index for one-active-review-per-submission-per-type constraint
alternatives_considered: Application-level check only: rejected because race conditions can create duplicate active reviews under concurrent requests.
Full unique index on (submission_id, review_type): rejected because a submission can have multiple reviews over its lifecycle (one per revision cycle), only one should be active at a time.
technical_decisions.justification: A partial unique index WHERE is_active = True guarantees at the database level that no two active reviews of the same type exist for a submission. Previous reviews are deactivated (is_active = False) when a new revision cycle begins.

technical_decisions.decision: Simple audit log table (ReviewAuditLog) instead of event sourcing
alternatives_considered: Event sourcing with event store: rejected for v1 — overkill for the current scale, adds infrastructure complexity (event store, projections, replay).
No audit log (reconstruct from Review history): rejected because reviews are mutable (decision field changes) and we need an immutable record.
technical_decisions.justification: An append-only audit log table provides the immutability and traceability required by NFR-4.1 with minimal infrastructure. The table uses no SoftDeleteMixin and the application layer prohibits UPDATE/DELETE. Can migrate to event sourcing in v2 if replay/projection needs arise.

technical_decisions.decision: SELECT FOR UPDATE row locking on submission status transitions
alternatives_considered: Optimistic locking with version field: viable but requires retry logic on the client side, adding complexity to the API contract.
No locking (application-level status check only): rejected — TOCTOU race between status check and status update.
technical_decisions.justification: SELECT FOR UPDATE provides pessimistic locking that guarantees only one transition executes at a time for a given submission. The lock is held only during the transaction (short-lived). This is the simplest correct solution for PostgreSQL.

technical_decisions.decision: Revision count tracked cumulatively on the Review record, not on the submission
alternatives_considered: Track on submission: rejected because if the submission model is owned by another service, we'd need cross-service state coordination.
Track as a derived count from audit log: rejected because COUNT queries under concurrent writes are unreliable for enforcement.
technical_decisions.justification: Storing revision_count on the Review record (carried forward to new reviews via the service layer) keeps the state local to the review domain. The service increments the count when creating a new review after a revision, and checks it before allowing revision_requested decisions.

data_flow.description: Full review cycle for a content submission, from brand review through compliance to publish readiness

steps.action: Creator submits content (handled by Content Submission Service)

steps.result: Brand sees the submission content and any existing reviews

steps: ReviewService acquires SELECT FOR UPDATE lock on submission
Creates Review(review_type=compliance_review, decision=pending) for the compliance stage
Dispatches Celery task: notify admin of new compliance queue item
Dispatches Celery task: notify creator with feedback
→ Creator revises and resubmits (new version), flow restarts at Step 2 with incremented revision_count
Dispatches Celery task: notify creator of rejection

steps.result: Admin sees list of submissions awaiting compliance review (FIFO)

steps: ReviewService acquires lock, validates submission.status == pending_compliance
Dispatches Celery task: notify creator to publish
Updates existing compliance Review(decision=rejected, rejection_reason=..., violation_category=...)
Dispatches Celery tasks: notify creator and brand of compliance rejection
→ Creator can revise and resubmit (flow restarts at Step 2 with incremented revision_count, re-entering brand review)

risk_assessment.risk: Review queue grows unbounded if brands are slow to review
risk_assessment.impact: Creator experience degrades, content becomes stale
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement reminder notifications (48h) and auto-escalation (7 days) via scheduled Celery beat tasks. P1 priority.

risk_assessment.risk: Compliance bottleneck — single compliance queue for all submissions
risk_assessment.impact: Compliance review becomes the slowest link in the chain
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor compliance queue depth. For v1, pooled queue with overdue flagging. V2 can add reviewer assignment and specialization.
Partition by created_at (monthly). Add TTL archival policy for entries older than 2 years. Ensure queries always filter by submission_id (indexed).
